First Set Of Interrogatories Filed By Government
In Philadelphia Class Action Medical Marijuana Suit

April 12, 1999

IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF PENNSYLVANIA
DEFENDANT’S FIRST SET OF INTERROGATORIES

Pursuant to Rule 33 of the Federal Rules of Civil procedure Defendant requests that each named plaintiff, individually, respond to each of the following interrogatories.

INSTRUCTIONS

A. The interrogatories contained herein inquire as to all information presently in the knowledge, possession, custody, or control of you or any agent or other person acting or to act on your behalf.

B. If in answering these interrogatories you encounter any ambiguity in construing either an interrogatory or a definition or instruction relevant to the inquiry contained within an interrogatory set forth the matter deemed ambiguous and the Construction selected or used in answering the interrogatory.

C. Each of the interrogatories must be answered in writing under oath within thirty days after service, as required by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 33. The interrogatories are, furthermore, continuing to the extent Rule 26 permits, and require supplemental responses when appropriate.

D. All interrogatories should be answered individually by each named plaintiff; i.e., each named plaintiff should produce a separate document responding to all interrogatories for particular plaintiff and each plaintiff1s response must be signed, under oath, by that plaintiff.

E. The masculine includes the feminine and vice-versa. The Singular includes the plural and vice-versa.

F. A request for the identification or description of any fact includes, without limitation, a request for the identification and description of all persons with knowledge of such fact.

G. In each instance where you deny knowledge or interrogatories sufficient to answer an interrogatory, please set forth the name and addresses of each person, if any, who are known by you to have such knowledge and in each instance where you aver insufficient knowledge or information as a grounds for not providing information requested by an interrogatory, please set forth a description of the efforts made to locate information needed to answer the interrogatory.

H. In the event that information sought in any interrogatory is withheld on the basis of privilege or any other objection, then as to such information allegedly subject to such asserted privilege or objection, you are requested to supply an identification of such information, in writing, with sufficient specificity to permit the court to reach a determination in the event of a motion to compel as to the applicability of the asserted privilege or objection, together with an indication of the basis for the assertion of the privilege or objection.

DEFNITIONS

A. In these interrogatories, the term "you" or "your" means each of the named plaintiffs, individually, as well as their agents, attorneys, and anyone acting or purporting to act their behalf.

B. "Person," unless otherwise specified, means a natural person, firm partnership, trust, estate, association, corporation, Proprietorship, governmental body, governmental agency or commission or any other organization or entity.

C. The term "identify" means, unless otherwise defined below, with respect to an individual, his or her full name, business title and responsibility, present or last known address and telephone number, and relationship to you. If you do not know all of the requested information for an individual, state as much of the requested information as you do know, and specify the reasons for not answering completely.

D. The term "marijuana" means all parts of the plant Cannabis sativa L., whether growing or not; the seeds thereof; the resin extracted from any part of such plant; and every compound, manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture, or preparation of such plant, its seeds or resin. see 21 U.S.C. § 802(16).

F. The term "smoked marijuana" means marijuana prepared in cigarette, cigar or pipe form.

F. The term ‘Marijuana Single patient IND Program" means the Department of Health and Human service1s single patient investigational new drug (IND) research process for smoked marijuana, and also means the compassionate Access Program as that term is used in Plaintiffs’ Second Amended Complaint and also means the Compassionate Use Program as that term is used in the district court’s Memorandum and order dated March 10, 1999.

G. The term "medical professional" includes but is not limited to any physician, nurse, psychiatrist, psychologist, or other professional health care provider.

Interrogatories

INTERROGATORY NO. 1: state your full name, present address and telephone number; and identify any other person contributing information to the answers of these interrogatories-

INTERROGATORY NO. 2: Identify every person whom you may call as a non-expert witness at the trial of this matter. With respect to each person, state the substance of the facts to which he or she may testify.

INTERROGATORY NO. 3: Identify those expert witnesses whom you may call at trial. With respect to each, state (i) their academic background and relevant experience; (ii) the subject matter on which the expert may testify; (iii) the substance of the facts and opinions to which the expert may testify; and (iv) a summary of the grounds for each opinion.

INTERROGATORY NO 4: List each specific medical, mental or physical condition, disability, illness, or disease for which you contend that you have benefited or will benefit from the use of smoked marijuana.

INTERROGATORY NO. 5: For each medical, mental or physical condition, disability, illness, or disease identified in interrogatory No. 2, above, state the following:

a. Whether you are currently under the care professional, and if so identify the medical.

b. What treatments, drugs or other remedies professional has prescribed or recommended.

c. Which of the above treatments, drugs or other remedies that your medical professional has prescribed or recommended you have utilized.

d. Whether any treatments, drugs or other remedies, with or without side effects, alleviate, relieve, or lessen your medical, mental or physical condition, disability, illness, or disease.

e. Whether you have used smoked marijuana.

f. Whether you are currently using smoked marijuana.

g. Whether you want to use smoked marijuana, but have not yet done so.

h. Whether the medical professional whose care you have sought has recommended that you use smoked marijuana.

i. Whether the medical professional whose care you have sought has approved of your use of smoked marijuana after you informed him that you have used it.

INTERROGATORY NO. 6: State whether you seek to solely use smoked marijuana, or marijuana in some other form in order to treat the medical, mental or physical condition, disability illness, or disease identified in response to Interrogatory No. 2, above.

INTERROGATORY NO 7: State whether you have ever requested that a medical professional apply to the Marijuana single Patient IND Program for smoked marijuana as a treatment for you, and if so state the medical professional’s response to your request.

INTERROGATORY NO. 8: Identify the medical professional referred to in response to Interrogatory No. 5, above.

INTERROGATORY NO. 9: state whether a medical professional has ever applied to the Marijuana single Patient IND Program for smoked marijuana as a treatment for you, and if so, state the date of the application and the disposition of the application, i.e., whether the application was approved, put on hold, or denied.

INTERROGATORY NO. 10: Identify the medical professional referred to in response to Interrogatory No. 7, above.

INTERROGATORY No. 11: Plaintiffs allege that "{in 1999 the Public Health service arbitrarily suspended the compassionate Access Program Indefinitely." Complaint, ¶ 193. Describe in detail the factual basis for your allegation that the Marijuana single Patient IND Program was "arbitrarily" suspended.

INTERROGATORY NO. 12: State whether you have been arrested/convicted for any marijuana offense, either state or federa1 and if so, state the offense and if convicted, the sentence or disposition.
(Marijuananews note: And if not, why not? Undoubtedly they would like to do whatever is necessary to fill that void in the patients’ lives.)
